name: nfdump
what_it_is: nfdump is a suite of tools for collecting, storing, and analyzing NetFlow, IPFIX, and sFlow network traffic data. It provides high-performance flow capture daemons, a filtering and aggregation engine, and enrichment utilities for network traffic analysis.
components: nfcapd — NetFlow collector daemon (v1/v5/v7/v9 and IPFIX)
nfpcapd — converts live traffic or pcap files to NetFlow records
nfdump — primary analysis tool for filtering and post-processing flows
nfreplay — replays stored NetFlow data to other collectors
nfanon — IP address anonymization using CryptoPAn algorithm
nfexpire — manages expiration of old flow data files
geolookup — enriches flows with geolocation and AS number data
torlookup — enriches flows with Tor exit node data
ft2nfdump — optional converter from flow-tools format
protocols: NSEL (Network Event Security Logging) via NetFlow v9
NAT Event Logging via NetFlow v9
measurement: Per-flow byte and packet counters (64-bit internal storage)
Automatic sampling rate recognition with byte/packet multiplication
Flow aggregation on any flow element or combination
Statistics generation over any flow element
IP geolocation and AS number annotation
Tor exit node detection per flow
Flexible output: text, CSV, JSON, custom format strings
configuration: Compression codec selection: LZ4, LZO, ZSTD, bzip2
Listening port for incoming flow streams
Custom library paths for compression dependencies
Optional JA4 fingerprinting module at build time
Optional ft2nfdump and JunOS modules at build time
modes: Collection mode — nfcapd/sfcapd listening on UDP ports for live flow data
Analysis mode — reading stored binary files with tcpdump-like filter expressions
Aggregation mode — user-defined grouping and summarization of flows
Enrichment mode — annotating flows with geolocation, AS numbers, or Tor status
Replay mode — nfreplay re-emitting stored flows to another collector
pcap conversion mode — nfpcapd reading pcap files or live interfaces
constraints: NetFlow v5/v7 use 32-bit on-wire counters; overflow risk on high-bandwidth links (mitigated by 64-bit internal storage)
Binary file format is architecture-dependent (endianness); files are not portable across big-endian/little-endian systems without conversion
Legacy nfdump-1.6.x file format is only readable by the nfdump binary, not by collector daemons
Root privileges required to bind collector daemons to ports below 1024
No built-in access control; network-level filtering must be handled by the host OS or firewall
notable_absences: No built-in graphical user interface (NfSen is a legacy separate project)
No real-time alerting or notification subsystem
No fault injection or traffic simulation capability
No built-in authentication or access control for the collector endpoints
